stories.headline: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Afghanistan: NCS
stories.title: 5.3 magnitude earthquake strikes Afghanistan: NCS
stories.summary: Kabul , October 1 : An earthquake of magnitude 5.3 struck Afghanistan on Thursday morning, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said. According to the NCS, the earthquake occurred at 6:59:20 am IST at a depth of 126 km. In a post shared on X, the NCS said, "EQ of M: 5.3, On: 01/10/2026 06:59:20 IST, Lat: 35.981 N, Long: 68.700 E, Depth: 126 Km, Location: Afghanistan." The NCS located the earthquake at latitude 35.981 North and longitude 68.700 East, around 165 km NNW of Kabul. Further details are awaited.

stories.title: Pakistan's information minister criticises India's decision to hold IWT in abeyance
stories.summary: India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025, a day after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people, saying it would remain suspended until Pakistan takes credible action against cross-border terrorism
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'terror attack' in summary weight 50.4
article_sentences: Pakistan's Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Wednesday criticised India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance, saying it was a binding pact.

The IWT of 1960 is a World Bank-brokered agreement between India and Pakistan that governs the sharing of the waters of the six rivers of the Indus basin, allocating the eastern rivers to India and the western rivers largely to Pakistan.

India placed the treaty in abeyance in April 2025, a day after the Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people, saying it would remain suspended until Pakistan takes credible action against cross-border terrorism.
Addressing an event organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, Tarar said that the IWT was legally binding.

He said that the treaty cannot be “unilaterally altered, revoked, rescinded or held in abeyance, for that matter, but even if there is a dispute, both the parties have to adhere to the terms and conditions of the treaty”.
The minister warned that Indian action to suspend the treaty would have global implications.
Tarar reiterated that Pakistan will continue to engage the international community and defend the country’s vital national interests.
“We are a peaceful nation, but we cannot allow India to weaponise water because it is the basic right of the 240 million people of Pakistan,” Tarar said.

stories.headline: LeT commander’s killing big blow to terror network: MHA
stories.title: LeT commander’s killing big blow to terror network: MHA
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 30: A senior and wanted Lashkar-e-Taiba commander was killed in an intelligence-led joint operation in the Gurwatkalan area of Khansahib in Budgam district, security officials said on Wednesday, bringing an end to a sustained hunt for the wanted terrorist. The slain terrorist has been identified as Muhammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa. According to an official statement issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs, security forces had been pursuing Musa for a considerable period and recently put in place a coordinated plan for his neutralisation after receiving technical and human intelligence about his movement and presence in the area. “The operation was carried out jointly by the Indian Army, Jammu and Kashmir Police and CRPF,” it said. In a series of posts on X, based on specific intelligence input, a joint search operation was launched by the army, J&K police and the CRPF in the general area of Korag, Yousmarg. “Vigilant troops observed suspicious activity and upoun being challenged, terrorists opened fire, prompting a fierce exchange of gunfire during which one terrorist was killed,” the post read. In another post, the army said: “Further to the ongoing operation, during the search early morning in general area Palmaidan, body of Pakistan based LeT terrorist, identified as Mohammad Asif alias Hashim Moosa, was recovered along with war like stores.” The operation comes weeks after another encounter in the same district in which Musa’s close associate Yasir alias Abu Talha was killed. As per the officials, Yasir was neutralised on September 4 during Operation Asdhar in the Budgam forests. The proximity of the two operations formed part of the continuing security forces’ effort to track the group operating in the forested areas of central Kashmir. The MHA in its official statement said that Musa’s killing completes the neutralisation of a group of four senior Lashkar-e-Taiba commanders who had been operating in J&K in 2022 and had been linked by security agencies to several major attacks. The other three commanders identified by the government were Junaid Bhat, killed in Dachigam in December 2024; Suleman, killed during Operation Mahadev in July 2025; and Yasir, killed in Budgam earlier this month. The government has linked the group to a series of attacks, including the Halan, DKG, Kandi, Shahsitar, Shiv Khori, Gagangir, Bootapathri and Baisaran attacks. The Ministry described Musa’s killing as a serious setback to the Lashkar-e-Taiba network in J&K. The latest operation also underscores the continued focus of security agencies on the forest belts of central Kashmir, where difficult terrain and mobility have complicated counter-terror operations. The Ministry said the operation formed part of an ongoing, long-sustained counter-terrorism effort, with different security agencies working in coordination across Jammu and Kashmir. With Musa’s killing, officials said, the four-member senior LeT command group identified as having operated in the region since 2022 has been neutralised. The operation in Budgam comes against the backdrop of intensified searches and encounters in the district in recent weeks, including the September operation in which Yasir was killed, highlighting the continued security focus on the forested upper reaches of the district.

stories.headline: Dynamic leaders powering India’s future
stories.title: Dynamic leaders powering India’s future
stories.summary: India's growth story today is being written not just by policies and markets, but by the individuals steering change from the front. Across industries — from technology and finance to healthcare, infrastructure, and manufacturing — a new generation of visionary leaders is reshaping how business gets done, blending bold ambition with grounded execution. These are the changemakers who see opportunity where others see obstacles, who build institutions rather than just companies, and who are quietly setting the tone for India's economic trajectory in the years ahead. This feature spotlights a few such names driving impact, innovation, and inspiration nationwide.Umashankar SudarsanUmashankar Sudarsan, Founder & CEOWhy Enterprise Transformation Starts With Trusted Data Umashankar, Founder and CEO of AppBeez Infotech and Infiniqon Technologies, brings more than three decades of experience in enterprise technology. His expertise spans revenue management, billing, CPQ, data governance, and technology modernization. As organizations invest in AI and automation, he sees data quality as a leadership responsibility. Inconsistent information can undermine decisions, disrupt operations, and limit the value of new technology. Lasting transformation depends on clear ownership of data and the discipline to keep it accurate, consistent, and accessible.For Umashankar, innovation should produce measurable outcomes: more reliable operations, better informed decisions, and value that endures as organizations grow. He also mentors and invests in early-stage technology companies, with interests in AI, cloud infrastructure, and data platforms.His broader vision connects responsible technology adoption with India’s Viksit Bharat 2047 ambition, emphasizing the digital capabilities and institutional trust needed for sustainable growth.Vipul B Varshneya and Anuj VarshneyaVipul B Varshneya (MD) & Anuj Varshneya (Co-Founder & Director) With over 40 years of experience,their architecture has transformed spaces for generations. With a focus on designing spaces that inspire, the goal is to use architecture to create a lasting impact on communities and the environment.Their founded company, STHAPATI is a multidisciplinary architectural practice headquartered in Lucknow and New Delhi. Their portfolio spans a spectrum of building typologies, from housing to large-scale urban developments across India and the globe—including the United States, New Zealand and Mauritius . A leader in airport terminal design and public infrastructure, they are also known for master planning, commercial, institutional, and heritage projects — delivering design solutions that are visionary and rooted in context like IITs,embassies and central universities. The projects seamlessly blend regional influences with cutting edge technology to craft universally relevant spaces.At present Harsh Varshneya and Khushboo bansal are spearheading the company with the commitment to responsible architecture which drives to develop solutions that are both sustainable and forward-thinking, resilient, adaptable, and impactful.Ashish V. KhemkaAshish V. Khemka, Chairman & Managing DirectorAshish V. Khemka comes from a third-generation entrepreneurial family with roots in the tea and timber businesses but chose to carve out his own path in pharmaceuticals.More than two decades ago, he founded AMN Life Science with an ambition to build beyond the domestic market, focusing from the outset on international expansion, strong manufacturing capabilities and long-term partnerships.That approach has shaped how he has grown AMN over the years. Under his leadership, the company has expanded to three manufacturing facilities, including two finished dosage formulation plants and one API facility, and built a presence across more than 50 countries.Today, AMN has over 1,000 registered products and 150 EU Marketing Authorisations, with regulatory capabilities spanning the EU, UK, Canada and Australia. As the business has grown, Mr. Khemka has continued to expand its capabilities through integrated CDMO and CMO solutions, building AMN into a global pharmaceutical partner.Dr. Raju DesaiDr. Raju Desai , Chairman & Managing DirectorFor more than four decades, Dr. Raju Desai has been closely associated with the evolution of India’s plastics manufacturing industry. As Chairman & Managing Director of Jyoti World and President of Plastindia Foundation for 2026–28, he brings an industry perspective shaped by manufacturing, technology and global markets.His leadership at Jyoti World reflects a broader belief: India’s manufacturing opportunity lies not only in scale, but in deeper capabilities. The company has built an integrated ecosystem spanning polymer compounding, tooling, injection moulding, profile extrusion, machining and product development, enabling it to work with global OEMs on increasingly complex applications.Today, Dr. Desai’s focus extends beyond manufacturing capacity to the larger ecosystem by encouraging technology adoption, sustainable materials, skill development and stronger industry collaboration. Through his leadership, he continues to advocate for an Indian plastics industry that is globally competitive, technologically progressive and responsible in its growth.Smita ChatterjiSmita Chatterji, Founder & Group CEO Smita Chatterji has built a life across worlds that are too often treated as separate. A painter, philanthropist and homemaker, she is also a first-generation entrepreneur and the founder and Group CEO of Centreax, a technology company with offices in Kolkata, Chennai and Manila.Under her leadership, Centreax has developed digital solutions across banking, insurance, healthcare, education, agriculture, manufacturing, retail and hospitality. Its AI-powered platform CentraDox brings greater clarity and accountability to enterprise decisions by keeping approvals, documents and the reasoning behind them connected.Chatterji’s range of experience shapes the way she leads. She brings an artist’s attention to design, a homemaker’s understanding of competing demands and an entrepreneur’s determination to solve problems. A former chair of CII’s Indian Women Network in West Bengal, she also supports women entrepreneurs and wider opportunities in Eastern India. Her story makes a compelling case for leadership built from more than one identity.Prashant TiwariPrashant Tiwari, ChairmanMr. Prashant Tiwari, Chairman of Prateek Group, is a first-generation entrepreneur and Civil Engineer who founded Prateek Group in 2005 with a vision to create landmarks and set new benchmarks in real estate. Over more than two decades, he has steered the company into a trusted name in North India's real estate sector, driven by an unwavering commitment to quality construction, timely delivery and thoughtful design. His leadership rests on strong values of transparency, robust engineering and a customer-first approach. Under his guidance, the group has delivered landmark residential and commercial projects across the NCR, including developments in Noida and Ghaziabad, alongside a 40-acre integrated township. Mr. Tiwari continues to push the boundaries of premium luxury and fine living, believing that the sky is the limit, and remains focused on creating lasting relationships built on trust, commitment and consistently delivered promises.Dr. Mohana Rao PatibandlaDr. Mohana Rao Patibandla, Founder & CEODr. Mohana Rao Patibandla: Advancing World-Class Neurosurgical Care from Guntur An internationally trained neurosurgeon and healthcare entrepreneur, Dr. Mohana Rao Patibandla is Founder & CEO of Dr. Rao’s Hospital – International Institute of Neurosciences (IIN), Guntur, one of India’s leading standalone institutes dedicated to advanced brain, spine, stroke, and nerve care. Following his neurosurgery training at Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS), Hyderabad, he pursued fellowships across the United States spanning skull base surgery, pediatric neurosurgery, neuro-oncology, cerebrovascular and endovascular neurosurgery, functional stereotactic radiosurgery, and minimally invasive techniques. His research has earned global recognition, including the Brainlab Neurosurgery Best Paper Award at the Congress of Neurological Surgeons (CNS), USA, Best Paper honours at MISSABCON and PASMISSCON, and the COSSCON Gold Medal for spine surgery research. An International Member of the American Association of Neurological Surgeons (AANS) and Member of CNS, USA, Dr. Rao remains dedicated to bringing globally benchmarked, evidence-based neurosurgical care to India while advancing innovation, education, and patient outcomes.Dr. Neelanjan MannaDr. Neelanjan Manna, CTODr. Neelanjan Manna: Building India’s Digital Future from First PrinciplesBorn in South Kolkata in 1997, Dr. Neelanjan Manna’s path from dismantling household electronics to pioneering deep-tech innovation embodies India’s self-reliance ambitions. Shaped by a freedom- fighter grandfather’s rebellious spirit and a businessman grandfather’s pragmatism, he pursued cryptography and computer science at VIT, publishing the “Manna Cipher” in 2020.When the pandemic disrupted conventional career paths, Manna founded SciFii Inc. from a modest room in his family home, focusing on offline functionality and data sovereignty. He now serves as Managing Director at Dortrees Technologies Private Limited, driving initiatives in AI, quantum computing, blockchain and indigenous cryptographic research, including forensic and deepfake - detection tools under Project XEUS.Rejecting opportunities abroad to counter brain drain, Manna champions homegrown intellectual property over imported technology. He mentors innovators in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and authored the autobiography "Reinventing the Wheel. Named among India’s Most Inspiring AI Leaders in 2025, he continues building technology that positions India as a creator, not merely a consumer, of global innovation.Kunal MittalKunal Mittal, CEOBuilding Business Bridges Through the India–UK FTAKunal Mittal, CEO, Akash Coke Industries Pvt. Ltd. represents a new generation of Indian entrepreneurs who see opportunity not merely in individual sectors, but in the intersections between businesses, markets and economies. With entrepreneurial interests spanning coal, steel, hospitality and other ventures, Mittal brings a diversified and pragmatic perspective to the evolving India–UK business relationship.For him, the India–UK Free Trade Agreement is more than a reduction in tariffs—it is a catalyst for cross-border enterprise. Greater market access can create new possibilities for Indian businesses across manufacturing, metals, hospitality, technology, services and consumer industries, while opening avenues for strategic partnerships and investment.Mittal believes the real opportunity lies in thinking beyond traditional exports. Joint ventures, global supply chains, technology collaborations and international expansion can help Indian enterprises build scale and competitiveness.His approach is distinctly entrepreneurial: identify emerging opportunities early, build strong partnerships and turn changing trade dynamics into sustainable business growth.The pages slugged ‘Brand Connect’ are equivalent to advertisements and are not written and produced by Forbes India journalists.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(September 30) criticised the Uttar Pradesh police for registering a first information report against an unknown person in a case of motorcycle theft, despite the fact that the complainant had apprehended the thief on the spot.

In a case before Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva, the complainant appeared in person and alleged that despite him informing the UP Police about the person who stole his motorcycle, the police registered an FIR and left the column for adding the name of the accused person blank.
He stated that it was only after she approached the Allahabad High Court that the police added the name of an unknown person as accused.
The complainant ultimately had to knock on the doors of the Supreme Court.
When the matter came up here, the Court had asked the UP Police to file an affidavit in this regard, which was filed by Shobit Kumar, Circle, Khurja, Bulandshahr, UP.
However, the Court found the affidavit to be "utterly uninspiring" because it clearly revealed the FIR was supplemented with the accused's name later.
Questioning how an investigating agency could break the trust of the people, Justice Kumar asked the Circle Officer to be present in the next hearing.
"We find the affidavit dated 25.09.2026 filed by Mr. Shobhit Kumar, Circle Officer, Khurja, Bulandsahr, Uttar Pradesh, to be utterly uninspiring.
The said officer shall be present before this Court on the next date of hearing to account for the same.

It would be open to him to file a better affidavit explaining as to why First Information Report No. 195/2026 was registered on 19.08.2026 against an unknown motorcycle rider when it is the admitted fact that the said motorcycle rider was apprehended at the spot.
In paragraph 6 of the aforestated affidavit, the name of the motorcycle rider is disclosed as Tushar s/o Sh.
Prempal.
